Understanding React Server Components

React Server Components (RSC) are a new type of component that runs exclusively on the server. They allow you to write components that have access to the server environment directly.1

Key Benefits

  • Zero client-side JavaScript — Server components don't add to your bundle size
  • Direct backend access — Query databases, read files, access secrets
  • Automatic code splitting — Client components are automatically code-split

Example

// This component runs on the server only
async function ProductList() {
  const products = await db.query('SELECT * FROM products');
  return (
    <ul>
      {products.map(p => (
        <li key={p.id}>{p.name} - ${p.price}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
Server Components cannot use hooks like useState or useEffect. Use client components for interactive UI.

JavaScript

Copy response and toggle feedback.

HTML
// Copy response content
document.querySelectorAll('.zak-copy-response').forEach(btn => {
    btn.addEventListener('click', function() {
        const response = this.closest('.zak-ai-response');
        const text = response.querySelector('p, h2, ul, pre')
            .closest('.zak-ai-response').textContent.trim();
        navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
        this.innerHTML = 'âœ“ Copied';
        setTimeout(() => this.innerHTML = 'ðŸ“‹ Copy', 2000);
    });
});

// Feedback toggle
document.querySelectorAll('.zak-ai-response-feedback button').forEach(btn => {
    btn.addEventListener('click', function() {
        const sibling = this.parentElement.querySelector(
            this.classList.contains('zak-feedback-up') ? '.zak-feedback-down' : '.zak-feedback-up'
        );
        sibling?.classList.remove('active');
        this.classList.toggle('active');
    });
});
